proportion_bench.name: Proportion Bench
proportion_bench.description: One right triangle drawn on a 1.09 x 1.006 m slate, at a hypotenuse of 0.450 m that does not change. Four proportions - righttriangle's own isoceles, 3-4-5, 1-2 and kepler, its four values in its order - and because the hypotenuse is held constant they are four shapes at one size rather than four sizes, which is the opposite of what righttriangle does (it holds the longer LEG at 1.0, so its four hypotenuses run from 1.118 to 1.414). Three readings, from mute to demonstrated: `figure` is the triangle as one chalk slab and nothing else; `marks` puts righttriangle's own notation on it, cyan legs against a pink hypotenuse with the draughtsman's square at the right angle; `squares` erects real square slabs on all three sides, pythagorean_triangle_angles' proof-picture, so that 0.2025 square metres of blue and orange stands against 0.2025 square metres of purple in every one of the four cells. All four satisfy a^2 + b^2 = c^2, so the axis is not about geometry: 3-4-5 is the rope-stretcher's triangle you can tie in twelve knots, isoceles is the half-square whose hypotenuse the side cannot name, 1-2 is the half-domino that makes root five, kepler is the only right triangle whose sides are a geometric progression. Nothing animates, nothing is printed, nothing is random.
interactions: stand at reading=squares and put the four proportions side by side: the purple square never changes size, because the hypotenuse never changes - it is the same 0.2025 square metres four times while the blue and orange trade area between them
put 3-4-5 and kepler side by side at reading=figure: 36.870 degrees against 38.173, and the two triangles are very nearly one picture
then put the same two at reading=squares: the proof-picture magnifies the same 1.303-degree difference about sevenfold, because a square squares it
read the corner glyph across all four: it is the same size and in the same place in every cell, because the right angle is the one thing the axis cannot touch
count the sides at reading=marks: three cyan-and-pink figures with a pink bar of identical length, which is the normalisation stated as an object
proportion_bench.capacity: SEE that which right triangle counts as THE right triangle is a choice about what you can construct and what you find beautiful, not a fact about geometry - and that the choice of what to hold constant while comparing them is a second choice of the same kind

spatial_needs.footprint_note: Every single-layout cell is the SAME body: a 1.090 x 1.006 x 0.020 m slate turned to face bearing 0.62 rad, with the drawing standing at most 0.026 m proud of it, so the world box is 0.914 x 1.006 x 0.671 and one grid cell holds it. It is identical for all twelve cells by construction - the slate and its rebate are drawn before either axis is consulted. layout=ladder stands all four proportions in a row at 1.20 m pitch (about 4.5 m wide) and is a design view, not a map placement.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry in a Python replica built from the same constants; no Godot was run. The box is the SLATE plus the 26 mm relief, rotated by FRONT_YAW 0.62: 1.090 cos 0.62 + 0.046 sin 0.62 = 0.914 in x, 1.090 sin 0.62 + 0.046 cos 0.62 = 0.671 in z, y from BASE_Y 0.050 to 1.056. IDENTICAL for all twelve cells, which is the whole reason a triangle that draws 3.7 percent of the slate and a proof that draws 41.5 percent frame the same.

dna.default: proportion=isoceles, reading=figure. Both are righttriangle's shipped defaults under this bench's names: its @export default is `proportion: String = "isoceles"` (gd:31) with `reading: String = "uniform"` (gd:32), and `uniform` is exactly what `figure` builds - the triangle as one mute slab with no notation and no squares, which is the mesh righttriangle's 16 placements have always drawn. `isoceles` is also the case its pre-promotion code hard-coded, both legs pinned to triangle_size. So the default cell of this synthesis is the centre member's own default triangle drawn the way the centre member draws it. It is NOT the largest subject - `squares` draws about nine times the area - but framing is solved on the slate, which is identical in every cell, so the choice of default costs the sweep nothing.
dna.note: WHAT THE VALUES MEAN, from the members' code. THE FAMILY FIRST: four artifacts argue about the triangle and each holds a DIFFERENT thing still. righttriangle holds the RATIOS (proportion: isoceles | 3-4-5 | 1-2 | kepler, LEG_RATIOS gd:38-43) and is the centre of this synthesis. invariants_demo holds the SHAPE (figure: equilateral | right | scalene, _verts_for_figure gd:96-113) and asks what survives a motion; its `right` case is the isoceles one, verts (-0.15, 0.35), (0.15, 0.35), (-0.15, 0.65), legs 0.30 and 0.30. pythagorean_triangle_angles holds the PROOF (evidence: result | trace | longhand | axiom) and asks how much of it is on show; `result` grows the three squares from the three sides, update_square_mesh gd:292-304. quad_line_puzzle holds the CONSTRAINT (figure: square | rectangle | rhombus | trapezoid, FIGURES gd:53-62) and asks which one you drop. Ratios, shape, proof, constraint. This bench takes the first as its main axis and the third as one rung of its second, and declines the other two (see declines). PROPORTION, four values, righttriangle's own four, character for character and in its order, at a HYPOTENUSE OF 0.450 M that never changes. isoceles = the half-square: legs 1 : 1, sides 1 : 1 : sqrt(2), acute angles 45.000 and 45.000, legs 0.318198 and 0.318198 m, area 0.050625 m^2. Its hypotenuse is the first length the side cannot name, and righttriangle's own note says so ('the metre grid cannot name my longest side'). It is also the only one of the four with a mirror symmetry, which is what makes it the flattering case in exactly invariants_demo's sense - a symmetric figure hides which measurement belongs to which side. 3-4-5 = the Egyptian rope-stretcher's triangle: legs 3 : 4, sides 3 : 4 : 5, acute angles 36.8699 and 53.1301, legs 0.270000 and 0.360000 m, area 0.048600 m^2. Twelve knots in a closed loop pulled taut at 3, 4 and 5 - the only one of the four you can BUILD with no measuring instrument, which is its whole claim and the thing this bench's normalisation takes away from it (see below). 1-2 = the half-DOMINO, a 1 x 2 rectangle cut on its diagonal: legs 1 : 2, sides 1 : 2 : sqrt(5), acute angles 26.5651 and 63.4349, legs 0.201246 and 0.402492 m, area 0.040500 m^2. NOT the half-square - that is isoceles, and the brief for this artifact said half-square; the code says 0.5 against 1.0 and the code wins. sqrt(5) is the point: it is the straightedge construction of the golden ratio, phi = (1 + sqrt(5)) / 2, so this value and `kepler` are the same number two moves apart. righttriangle's own comment says '1-2 generates root five' and it is right. kepler = the golden triangle: legs 1 : sqrt(phi), sides 1 : sqrt(phi) : phi, acute angles 38.1727 and 51.8273, legs 0.278115 and 0.353768 m, area 0.049194 m^2. It is the UNIQUE right triangle whose three sides are a geometric progression - if the sides are a, ar, ar^2 then 1 + r^2 = r^4, so r^2 = phi and r = sqrt(phi), one solution and no others. The brief asked whether righttriangle's kepler really is 1 : sqrt(phi) : phi and it IS, exactly: its literal 0.7861513777574233 is 1/sqrt(phi) and squares to 0.618034 = 1/phi, so the legs are 1/phi and 1/sqrt(phi) of the hypotenuse and they sum in square to 1 to twelve decimal places. And the same literal SURVIVES the renormalisation unchanged - it is short/long in righttriangle and long/hypotenuse here - which is not a coincidence but the definition of a geometric progression, and it is the check that the transcription is faithful. THE ONE THING I CHANGED, and it is the load-bearing decision. righttriangle normalises the LONGER LEG to 1.0 (its own comment, gd:37: 'normalised so the longer leg is always 1.0 - the footprint never grows'), so its four triangles share a leg and their HYPOTENUSES differ: sqrt(2) = 1.4142, 1.25, sqrt(5)/2 = 1.1180, sqrt(phi) = 1.2720, a 26.5 percent spread, with areas 0.500 / 0.375 / 0.250 / 0.393. Four different sizes, so its axis confounds shape with size. This bench holds c = 0.450 instead, and the four become commensurable: the longest side is one length, the areas run 0.0405 to 0.0506, and the only thing left moving is shape. THAT IS ITSELF A CLAIM AND SOMEONE CAN REFUSE IT. Holding c still privileges the side the theorem DERIVES; holding a leg still privileges the side you can lay out with a ruler. The normalisation buys comparability and sells constructibility - at c = 0.450 the rope-stretcher's triangle has legs of 0.270 and 0.360 m, which is 3 and 4 of nothing, so the value whose entire argument is that it needs no measurement is the one this bench can only reach by measuring. READING, three values, the ladder from mute to demonstrated that BOTH source families already carry (righttriangle uniform -> corner_marked -> legs_hypotenuse; pythagorean axiom -> result -> longhand). figure = righttriangle's `uniform`: the triangle as one chalk slab, 16 mm proud of the slate, naming nothing. 3.7 to 4.6 percent of the slate depending on the proportion. marks = righttriangle's `corner_marked` AND `legs_hypotenuse` in one figure - cyan bars on the two given sides, a pink bar on the derived third, and the white draughtsman's square at the right angle, all three colours lifted from its constants (gd:47-49). They are merged because at a constant hypotenuse the corner glyph alone changes under half a percent of the slate and would have been a null on its own; together they are the notation rung. 4.7 to 5.7 percent of the slate. THE GLYPH AND THE BAR WEIGHT ARE CONSTANT, not scaled by the legs as righttriangle scales them from min(bx, by) - which over these four values swings 58 percent. Here the mark that names the invariant is itself invariant, so every pixel of difference in this reading comes from the two vertices that actually moved, which is invariants_demo's claim turned into a construction rule. squares = pythagorean_triangle_angles' `result`: real square slabs erected outward on all three sides by its own rule (directed edge p1 -> p2, offset by perp = (edge.y, -edge.x), walked round a counter-clockwise triangle), in its own three colours - blue on leg a, orange on leg b, purple on the hypotenuse. 40.6 to 41.5 percent of the slate, about NINE TIMES the figure reading, and the theorem is a pixel count in it: 0.2025 m^2 of blue and orange against 0.2025 m^2 of purple, in every one of the four cells. The source draws its squares as alpha-0.3 planes; here they are opaque slabs, because a still cannot see through transparency the way a headset can. EXTENTS, since the readings are so unequal. Drawn figure per cell: at `figure` isoceles 0.318 x 0.318, 3-4-5 0.270 x 0.360, 1-2 0.201 x 0.402, kepler 0.278 x 0.354; at `marks` the same plus 11 mm of bar on each outer side; at `squares` isoceles 0.955 x 0.955, 3-4-5 0.990 x 0.900, 1-2 1.006 x 0.805, kepler 0.986 x 0.910. The union of all twelve is 1.0389 x 0.9546, the stage was sized for THAT (slate 1.090 x 1.006, 25.6 mm of margin all round), and the right angle is pinned so the union is centred on it. The slate and its rebate are drawn before either axis is consulted, so the AABB is 0.914 x 1.006 x 0.671 in every cell and the critic's crop - the union of two frames' subject boxes - is the same rectangle for every pair in the sheet. Every number below therefore has the same denominator, which is the only reason they can be compared at all. THE THESIS SOMEONE COULD DISAGREE WITH: which right triangle counts as THE right triangle is a cultural choice, not a geometric one, because all four satisfy the same theorem and differ only in what they make easy - a rope, a mirror, a root, a proportion. The disagreement available, and it is a good one: the four ARE geometrically distinct, the angles differ by up to 18.4 degrees, and calling that 'culture' is a way of not saying that 3-4-5 is simply the one with the smallest integers. The (3-4-5, kepler) cell is where that objection is sharpest - 1.303 degrees apart, one of them the cheapest triangle to build and the other the most expensive to justify, and at reading=figure they are very nearly one picture.

predicted_degeneracy.pair: 3-4-5 against kepler, in the figure reading
predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: Rasterised BEFORE ANY CAPTURE in the critic's own currency: the twelve cells rebuilt in Python from the same constants (same ratios, same origin, same slate, same bar weights), sampled on a 1000 x 1000 grid over the slate face, flat-filled with the greyscale each material lands at after artifact_dna_critic's per-frame background neutralisation, then diffed with its own diff() - mean over the crop for `frame`, mean of the hottest 5 percent for `focus`. The crop is the slate in every cell by construction, so the denominator is constant. WHY THIS PAIR. Hold c and the triangle is one angle. The four acute angles are 26.5651 (1-2), 36.8699 (3-4-5), 38.1727 (kepler) and 45.0000 (isoceles), so the six gaps are 1.3028, 6.8273, 8.1301, 10.3048, 11.6077 and 18.4349 degrees - and 3-4-5 to kepler is FIVE TIMES tighter than the next one up. In area: the two triangles share the right angle and both leg directions, their hypotenuses cross at (0.1016, 0.2245) from the slate centre, and the symmetric difference is the two slivers on either side of that crossing - 0.5 x 0.0081153 x 0.2245 plus 0.5 x 0.0062319 x 0.1016 = 0.0009116 + 0.0003165 = 0.0012276 m^2, which is 0.112 percent of the 1.09654 m^2 slate. Spread over the hottest 5 percent at a chalk-against-slate delta of about half of full scale gives 1.27 percent focus / 0.064 percent frame. Predicted 1.3. AND IT IS VERY NEARLY A DOUBLE ENTRY: the same pair at reading=marks is predicted 1.32 percent, because the notation is constant by construction and adds almost nothing to this axis - if those two rows differ by more than about 0.2 points, the marks are carrying signal they were built not to carry. FULL PREDICTED SHEET, focus percent / frame percent. reading=figure: 3-4-5/kepler 1.27/0.064, isoceles/kepler 6.29/0.315, isoceles/3-4-5 7.52/0.376, 3-4-5/1-2 11.17/0.559, 1-2/kepler 12.37/0.618, isoceles/1-2 17.82/0.891; mean 9.41. reading=marks: 1.32/0.066, 6.40/0.320, 7.67/0.383, 11.38/0.569, 12.60/0.630, 18.17/0.908; mean 9.59. reading=squares: 3-4-5/kepler 8.74/0.437, isoceles/kepler 35.62/2.162, isoceles/3-4-5 36.85/2.583, 3-4-5/1-2 37.70/3.100, 1-2/kepler 38.70/3.512, isoceles/1-2 42.16/5.526; mean 33.29 - the axis saturates here, because a square squares the difference and one square slab is already 18 percent of the slate. Axis means: proportion 17.43 focus / 1.60 frame, reading 31.48 focus. reading pairs at fixed proportion: figure/marks 11.80 to 12.24, figure/squares 41.18, marks/squares 41.18. THE HEADLINE WILL BE A PEAK AND IT WILL BE ABOUT `squares`. proportion reads 9.4 percent at figure and 33.3 at squares for the same four triangles - a 3.5x spread on one axis - so the sheet's peak says almost nothing about the axis and everything about which reading it was measured in. Read the per-pair rows. TWO NUMBERS TO CHECK BEFORE BELIEVING ANYTHING: (a) figure/marks is predicted at 12.2 percent, which sits exactly on the WEAK/BITES bar. At righttriangle's own bar weight (12 mm rather than 22) the same pair rasterises at 6.6 percent - a WEAK verdict on a reading that is obviously a different picture to a human eye - so the bars were widened to 22 mm on the strength of that trial and the note says so rather than pretending 22 was a drawing decision. If the capture comes back under 6 percent there, the marks did not build. (b) at reading=squares every pair except 3-4-5/kepler should land between 35 and 43 percent; if any of them lands under 20, the squares are not being erected outward and are overlapping the figure. THE PREDICTION IS A FLOOR. The replica has one flat fill per material, no light, no shadow, no antialiasing and no tonemap, and every prior prediction in this corpus under-read by 1.5x to 6.7x. If the sweep comes back BELOW 1.3 percent on the named pair, stop: check tools/check_dna_declarations.py first, then _rejects.json. NOTE THAT THE tier_terrarium TRAP CANNOT FIRE HERE and this was checked rather than assumed: cabinet_sweep.coerce() numericises anything that parses, but int('3-4-5'), float('3-4-5'), int('1-2') and float('1-2') all raise, so every value of this axis reaches the artifact as a String and Object.set() on a typed String property cannot be silently refused. rule_bench's `rule` axis does NOT have that protection and depends on capture_config_sweep's enum-hint conversion; this one does not.

dna.designed_nulls_why: THERE IS NO CONSTRUCTION-IDENTICAL PAIR IN THIS FAMILY, and registering one would be a lie. rule_bench could register (90, 218) because two different lookup tables emit the same wall from the same seed - a genuine collision in the mechanism. Four distinct ratios are four distinct triangles: no two of the twelve cells share a vertex position, and the tightest pair in the sheet is predicted at 1.27 percent, which is a measurement and not an identity. So the negative control here is the ABSENCE of a null, and it is a stronger one than a single declared pair: all 66 pairs in the sheet must be non-zero, and a 0.00 percent anywhere means the sweep did not set what it says it set. Read _rejects.json before reading the design. What IS constant by construction is inside each frame rather than between two of them, which is why none of it can be registered above, and each of the three is checkable from a single tile: (1) the slate and its rebate, 1.090 x 1.006 x 0.020 m, drawn before either axis is consulted, so the subject bounding box and the critic's crop are the same rectangle in all twelve cells; (2) the right-angle glyph and the bar weight in `marks`, 68 mm and 22 mm, NOT scaled from min(leg) as righttriangle scales them, so the mark that names the invariant is invariant - if the glyph changes size between two proportions, the constants were reconnected to the legs; (3) the hypotenuse itself, 0.450 m in every cell, which means the pink bar in `marks` is the same length four times and the purple square in `squares` is the same 0.2025 m^2 four times. That third one is the whole normalisation stated as an object, and it is the only claim in this artifact that a reader can falsify with a ruler.
dna.fixture_why: The bench can stand all four proportions in a row (layout=ladder, 1.20 m pitch, about 4.5 m wide) but the SWEEP must see one slate at a time: capture_config_sweep unions the AABB across a spec's variants, so a four-wide row in the same spec frames every single against four and a half metres and photographs it as a speck. layout is an export and NOT an axis - that is wave 13's lesson taken as a rule rather than relearned - and it ships at single, so the fixture is a belt over braces. NOTHING ELSE NEEDS FIXTURING, and the reason is worth recording: there is no time knob here and no randomness anywhere. Every vertex is arithmetic on four constants, the whole figure is built synchronously inside _ready, there is no _process, no Timer, no randf and no tween, so the frame is complete at frame one and two builds of one cell are the same mesh. The members' harness debt was not inherited because the members do not have any either - righttriangle and pythagorean_triangle_angles are both static, and pythagorean's only motion is a hand dragging a vertex.
dna.kin: righttriangle is the direct parent and this bench does not replace it: righttriangle is a REFERENCE FORM placed beside other geometry (its @identity: 'a reference form for right angles to which other geometry is compared', 16 placements across primitives and transformation), and it holds a leg constant because a reference has to keep its footprint. This bench holds the hypotenuse constant because a COMPARISON has to keep its scale. The two should NOT measure alike, and the difference between their two `proportion` sheets is the finding: same four values, same four names, and one of them will show size where the other shows shape. `reading` is a corpus word carried by at least three artifacts with three different value lists - righttriangle's uniform | corner_marked | legs_hypotenuse, rule_bench's spacetime | front | lookup, and this one's figure | marks | squares - and in every case it means the same thing, HOW FAR YOU ARE STANDING FROM THE CLAIM. That is the family this axis belongs to, and the mapping to the members is one line each: figure = righttriangle's uniform = pythagorean's axiom-with-the-figure-left-in; marks = corner_marked + legs_hypotenuse; squares = pythagorean's result. `evidence` (result | trace | longhand | axiom, 19 declarations) is the same question again with a fourth rung this bench does not have, and pythagorean_triangle_angles is the artifact to compare a `squares` tile against - those two SHOULD measure alike at that value, because it is the same construction from the same code. `proportion` is carried by nobody else in the corpus; the word is righttriangle's alone and is claimed here as a synthesis of it, not as a new vocabulary. triangle, pythagorean_triangle and parasol_triangle sit in the same directory and none of them declares an axis.
declines: invariants_demo's `pose` and quad_line_puzzle's `plane`, which is where this synthesis overrules its brief. The brief named four sources and implied all four should reach the axes. Two of them cannot: `pose` (none | translate | rotate | scale | shear | project) and `plane` (upright | ground) are both about HOW THE FIGURE IS PRESENTED, not what the figure is, and folding either one in would have made a third axis whose values move the whole drawing rather than the thing being compared - which is the fastest way to a sheet where every tile differs and no tile means anything. invariants_demo's own registry already says its `pose` argues 'which face of the argument this copy shows when you walk up'; that is a statement about staging, and this bench's staging is fixed on purpose so that the ratios are the only variable. What survives from those two is their QUESTION, not their values: invariants_demo asks what a motion cannot touch and the answer is built in as the constant right angle and the constant glyph; quad_line_puzzle asks which constraint you drop and the answer is that this axis drops none - all four values keep both the right angle and the closure, and vary only the ratio.

invariants_demo's `figure` (equilateral | right | scalene) as a second axis. It is the obvious move and it is wrong twice over. Only ONE of its three values is a right triangle, so two thirds of that axis would leave the family this bench is about; and its `right` case is legs 0.30 and 0.30, which is `isoceles` under another name, so the honest part of it is already a value of `proportion`. Adding it would have swept the same triangle twice and called the second one new.

pythagorean_triangle_angles' `trace` and `longhand` as further readings. They are the two best rungs of its ladder - the sliding shear and Euclid I.47 - and they are declined because they are a proof of the THEOREM, which is the thing all four proportions already share. A `longhand` tile would look almost identical across the four values by construction, which is a null with no argument in it: it would say only that the theorem holds, which is the premise of this artifact rather than a finding. What is taken instead is `result`, the one rung where the four proportions are visibly four different pictures of the same equality.

A fifth proportion. 1-3, 5-12-13, 8-15-17 and the 30-60-90 all suggested themselves and all are declined: 3-4-5 already carries the whole-number-rope argument and a second Pythagorean triple would only carry it again with worse integers, while 30-60-90 is the half-equilateral and would have imported invariants_demo's `equilateral` through a side door. righttriangle's list is four and it stays four - the only thing this synthesis adds to a member's declared vocabulary is nothing.

Scaling the notation from the legs, which is what righttriangle does (g = min(bx, by) * 0.18, t = min(bx, by) * 0.035, gd:144-150). Over these four values min(leg) swings 58 percent, so its glyph would grow and shrink with the proportion and the `marks` reading would be measuring the notation as well as the triangle. Constant here, and the cost is stated: it makes `marks` and `figure` nearly identical for the proportion axis (predicted 9.59 against 9.41 mean focus), which is the correct answer - notation carries no information about which triangle it is.

righttriangle's black. Its base_color is Color(0.1, 0.1, 0.1) and its @identity defends it as 'a neutral diagnostic color that does not compete with adjacent color coding', which is true in a lit room and false on capture_config_sweep's backdrop of Color(0.055, 0.055, 0.070). A black slab on a near-black ground is a null by accident. The polarity is inverted rather than the palette abandoned: the slate takes the dark (rule_bench's own BACK_COLOR), the figure takes the light, and every mark colour is righttriangle's or pythagorean's unchanged.

triangle_size, base_color and every other export the members carry. righttriangle exports both and this bench pins the scale to the hypotenuse instead - a larger or smaller triangle is a bigger photograph of the same claim. Neither is an export here.

Any caption, number, label or angle arc. pythagorean_triangle_angles prints 'a^2 + b^2 = c^2' with the arithmetic filled in and draws a yellow arc at each vertex; both are declined for postulate_bench's recorded reason - a printed 36.87 beside the figure makes the tile about typography, and the `squares` reading already states the equality in area, which is the form the source's own truth statement asks for ('the Pythagorean theorem is a statement about areas, not lengths').
dna.sweep_note: The full sheet is 4 x 3 = 12 and fits under build_dna_gallery's current default cap of 16, so --max=12 is stated for the record rather than because it is needed. It WOULD have been needed at the old default of 9, where `reading` is the later axis and gets trimmed from the tail until the cross product fits - at 9 the sheet renders as 4 x 2 and the `squares` reading, which is where the axis actually bites, does not exist. Check the cap before reading a flat verdict. The pre-registered closest pair lives at reading=figure, which is the FIRST value of the later axis and is never trimmed.
